paragraphs: Swamiji once compared human beings to silkworms.

A silkworm draws thread out of its own body and winds it around itself, layer after layer. In time, the cocoon it made becomes its prison. We do the same, he said: out of our own desires, habits and actions we weave the very bonds that hold us.

But the cocoon is not forever. Inside it, quietly, something is changing. In the same way, within our self-made limits we can grow towards spiritual realisation, and one day break out like a butterfly, completely free.
learn: Many of the walls around us, like bad habits, fears or narrow thinking, are ones we spun ourselves, which means we can also outgrow them. Treat difficult phases as a cocoon: a place to transform, not a place to stay.
